items.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So she joined the band, and she and Billie sat there on the bandstand.

ctx.x: How did . . . It would be good to know about how the record company worked with you at the time. Did you . . . did they dictate to you what you recorded?
No. I had a contract that says no-one could dictate. The contract stated that I had total autonomy over what I recorded. They didn’t have to release it, but they had to pay

me the advance. I didn’t know that they didn’t have to release it, or I’d have insisted on that too, because they wouldn’t release the Billie Holiday record of Any Old Time. But then I found out much later why that was. The real reason was that she had signed contracts with Brunswick and kept on signing them while she was with my band. I don’t know. So weird. Anyway, Brunswick raised hell when they heard the Victor record of Any Old Time. It had to be withdrawn. So then I let Helen Forrest sing it. Later, of…
